text: Management halted work on the previously announced company split and stopped incurring separation-related dis-synergies. The firm committed $600m to U.S. marketing, sales, R&D, and "product superiority/select pricing," keeping the merged structure intact while concentrating resources on a single operating plan under new CEO Steve Cahillane. Quarterly earnings beat estimates, while revenue missed.

meta.note: Tension between merger legacy and breakup logic remains unresolved.

text: January nonfarm payrolls rose 130,000 (above expectations and above revised December), while unemployment slipped to 4.3% and the broader U-6 measure fell to 8%. Gains were concentrated in health care (+82,000), social assistance (+42,000), and construction (+33,000), with declines in federal government (-34,000) and financial activities (-22,000). Average hourly earnings increased 0.4% m/m and 3.7% y/y; benchmark revisions cut prior jobs by 898,000.

meta.note: Establishment and household surveys moved in different magnitudes.

text: The FAA suddenly closed a 10-nautical-mile airspace ring around El Paso International Airport for "special security" reasons, halting flights until Feb. 20, then lifted the restriction hours later after a Defense Department action against cartel drones. The agency states there is "no threat to commercial aviation" and normal operations resumed, despite local and congressional objections to the lack of notice and coordination.

meta.note: Tension between security secrecy and aviation coordination shaped classification.

text: Pershing Square disclosed a Meta position equal to 10% of its capital, asserting the stock is undervalued despite planned $115-135B in 2026 AI capex. Ackman framed the stake as confidence in durable long-term earnings power, noting Meta trades at ~22x forward earnings versus higher multiples for peers.

meta.note: Market pricing and strategic conviction sit in tension without resolution.

text: Q4 EPS was $3.12 adjusted versus $3.05 expected, with revenue up 10% to $7.0B. Same-store sales rose 5.7% overall (6.8% in the U.S.) following renewed value menu and promotions. The company plans $3.7-3.9B in 2026 capex, adding about 2,100 net new restaurants (≈2.5% systemwide sales lift) while expecting a softer Q1 from winter disruptions.

meta.note: Promotional spikes (e.g., Grinch Meal) blur steady-state demand.

text: Cisco beat Q2 estimates (EPS $1.04 vs $1.02; revenue $15.35B vs $15.12) and reported 10% revenue growth with core networking up 21% to $8.3B, yet the shares fell ~7% after management guided only to in-line near-term results. FY26 targets imply ~8.5% revenue growth ($61.2-$61.7B) alongside $2.1B in AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers.

meta.note: Market reaction turned on guidance, not reported performance.

text: The House passed a 219-211 resolution to disapprove Trump's Canada tariffs after three Republicans helped defeat a rule that would have blocked debate. Several GOP members crossed the aisle despite presidential threats of electoral consequences, while Speaker Johnson argued Congress should not constrain the president during trade negotiations. The measure now goes to the Senate, where a veto is likely even if it passes.

meta.note: Conflict sits between constitutional roles and party loyalty rather than policy mechanics.
